title: Work-function-imprinted antiferroelectric ZrO2 nonvolatile cell
idea: Combine antiferroelectric ZrO2's double hysteresis (fatigue-resistant, 1e11+ cycles) with asymmetric electrodes, a TiN bottom and a high-work-function MoO3-capped top, whose built-in field shifts one AFE loop to straddle 0 V. The film then holds two remanent states at zero bias like a ferroelectric but switches through the gentler field-induced AFE transition.
why: Zero refresh with endurance beyond HZO FeRAM; a nonvolatile 1T1C at DRAM-like ~1 V using no tungsten, ruthenium or platinum.

title: Revival tournament: twelve forgotten storage elements on one common test chip
idea: Fund 12 revived storage elements (core, plated wire, bubble, parametron, CCD, Selectron and others) to a shared 1-Mb test vehicle with identical sense/IO periphery and one scorecard (fJ/bit, ns, F2, retention, endurance) on shared shuttle wafers, with kill-or-scale gates at 6 and 12 months and prize money for crossing DRAM-class thresholds.
why: Compares physics fairly at ~$2M per element instead of $100M+ per startup and compresses discovery time; attacks the capital and time chokepoints.

title: Electrowetting liquid-metal nanodroplet toggling between two chambers
idea: Adapt electrowetting displays and liquid lenses: seal a ~10 nm gallium-alloy droplet in a dual-chamber cavity with hydrophobic dielectric walls; voltage on one chamber electrode wets and pulls the droplet there, surface-tension pinning holds it, and a capacitance difference reads it.
why: Fact 3: state is held by interfacial energy rather than stored charge, so no refresh; non-destructive capacitive read removes restore energy (fact 8).

title: YMnO3 FeFET retried: improper ferroelectric resists depolarization when hot
idea: Late-1990s YMnO3 FeFETs died from leakage, charge injection and depolarization-limited retention. Use hexagonal YMnO3, whose polarization is improper (slaved to a lattice trimerization, Tc > 1000 K) so depolarization fields barely back-switch it, on a floating-metal MFMIS gate so the semiconductor never sees an injection field.
why: Keeps polarization at 125 C/10 y where proper ferroelectrics depolarize at scaled thickness, enabling a 1T nonvolatile gain-type cell.

title: Anodized-aluminum nanopores grow capacitor holes instead of etching them
idea: Scarcity rule: no high-aspect-ratio etch tool. Deposit an Al film over the cell transistors, imprint dimples at the storage-contact pitch, and anodize so self-ordered pores grow straight down at AR >150:1 by electrochemistry alone; ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines the pores as cup capacitors after the pore-bottom barrier is thinned to open each contact.
why: Reaches the AR ~115 needed for more charge (fact 1) without HAR dry-etch tools and hardmask stacks, cutting capital intensity (fact 4); pore-to-contact registration is the main risk.

title: STT-DRAM's shrinking-Delta killer fixed with tall shape-anisotropy free layers
idea: Samsung and Hynix STT-MRAM DRAM-replacement efforts stalled because interfacial anisotropy cannot keep Delta >= 60 at sub-20 nm diameters and 125 C. Make the free layer a 20-40 nm tall CoFeB/FeCo cylinder (aspect ratio >1.5), so perpendicular shape anisotropy, which falls only slowly with temperature, supplies the stability.
why: 125 C/10 y retention at ~10-15 nm diameter: 2-4x density over interfacial-PMA MTJs.

title: Shallow 1 fF pillars rescued by soft-decision sensing and LDPC
idea: Invert 'every cell must read correctly on its own' -> let cells be weak and the code be smart. Etch only 1 fF, AR ~15 pillars; sense amps emit 2-bit soft information (strong/weak 0/1) to an on-die LDPC decoder over 512-bit codewords, tolerating raw BER ~1e-3 that would kill a hard-decision chip.
why: Cuts capacitor AR 4-5x (fact 1) and lets refresh stretch since weak cells become erasures (fact 3), for ~12% parity plus decoder area; decoder latency is the risk.

title: Myelin sheath bitline: air-gap wrap raises cell-to-bitline transfer ratio
idea: Myelin wraps axons to cut their capacitance. Wrap each buried bitline in a sealed vacuum or air-gap sheath (k~1), segmented by short SiN 'nodes of Ranvier' for mechanical support, cutting bitline capacitance by ~40-50%.
why: Signal scales as Cs/(Cs+Cbl), so halving Cbl lets Cs fall ~40% at equal signal and the capacitor AR drop from ~70 to ~45 (fact 1). It also lowers bitline CV2 energy (fact 10).

title: III-nitride resonant-tunneling floating well: ns write, hour retention
idea: Scarcity rule: refresh is banned. Store electrons in a GaN quantum well clad by AlN barriers (~2 eV offset) so thermionic leakage is negligible, and write through an AlN/GaN/AlN double-barrier resonant-tunneling stack that conducts only when the gate aligns its resonant level near 1 V. Read through the HEMT channel that the stored charge depletes.
why: Kills the leakage-tail refresh tax (fact 3: 16-33% idle power, 10-20% bandwidth); cold resonant tunneling avoids hot-carrier damage for DRAM-class endurance; moves the ULTRARAM idea to wide-gap GaN-on-Si.

title: Chiral-molecule spin filter writes magnets with voltage, not current
idea: DNA and other chiral molecules spin-polarize the electrons that move through them (chiral-induced spin selectivity). Put a monolayer of helical oligopeptides on a thin perpendicular magnet. A gate voltage charge-polarizes the molecules, briefly creating a spin-polarized interface that tips the magnetization, so writing uses only displacement current.
why: Non-volatile magnetic bit written at fJ level, with no heavy-metal SOT lines (no W/Pt) and no MTJ breakdown. The molecules are cheap and solution-deposited.

title: ISS astronaut: directly grown 3R-MoS2 sliding-ferroelectric bit
idea: On the space station every drop is recycled, so there is no wet transfer. 3R-stacked bilayer MoS2 shows sliding ferroelectricity: the layers shift by one atomic registry to reverse polarization. Grow it directly on the BEOL by ~400 C MOCVD as a FeFET gate, with no water-bath transfer, PMMA strip or rinse.
why: Atom-thin, sub-1 V non-volatile switching attacks the voltage floor (fact 10) and refresh (fact 3). The storage layer is made entirely in gas-phase steps, with more than 10x less water.

title: Fatigue-free sliding ferroelectric bilayer for fifty-year deep-space probes
idea: Voyager-class probes need 50-year memory; MOCVD-grown bilayer MoS2 or hBN shows 'sliding' ferroelectricity in which polarization flips by a lateral interlayer shift without breaking bonds and shows no measurable fatigue. One mask patterns the BEOL bilayer into capacitors or FeFET gates over existing vias.
why: Atomically thin polarization storage with potentially unlimited endurance and sub-1 V switching (fact 10); wafer-scale control of bilayer stacking order is the risk.

title: On-die microheaters re-anneal worn cells every few hours at 350 C
idea: Embed a TiN heater serpentine under each memory mat. After ~1e10 cycles, migrate the mat's data and pulse it to ~350 C for ~10 ms to anneal out generated traps, vacancy clusters, ferroelectric imprint and MTJ barrier defects; the temperature stays inside the BEOL budget, so it heals without damage.
why: Converts finite-endurance elements (ferroelectric, ReRAM, charge-trap at 1e8-1e11 cycles) into effectively unlimited endurance, making them DRAM-class. Heater-based self-healing has been shown for NAND.

title: Airport baggage conveyor: vertical charge-coupled bit strings in 3D stacks
idea: Like bags riding a conveyor to one scanner, deposit a 3D-NAND-style stack of 64-128 gate layers around a vertical wide-gap channel (e.g., Ga2O3 or ZnSnO) and clock charge packets up and down it CCD-style; a single sense/restore node at the top of each string reads and rewrites packets as they pass. A bit is a potential well under a gate, so each tier costs one deposition, not a transistor plus capacitor.
why: Facts 2 and 4: 3D density without a 3D capacitor or lateral transistor; ~100 tiers at 3 gates/bit gives ~30 bits per hole, ~5-10x density with no added EUV; serial shift (~1 ns/stage) keeps average latency ~20-30 ns only if strings stay short.

title: Picosecond-switched hidden charge-density-wave state in 1T-TaS2 bits
idea: Cryogenic and ultrafast computing users exploit 1T-TaS2's metastable 'hidden' charge-density-wave state, entered by a ~30 ps electrical pulse and exited by a longer heating pulse, with 10-100x resistance contrast. Strain or doping engineering pushes the hidden state's lifetime from cryogenic toward room temperature for DRAM-like retention.
why: fJ-class picosecond switching (facts 5, 10) in a 2D layer stackable in BEOL; room-temperature retention is the speculative step.

title: Antiferromagnet Neel-vector bit with zero stray field
idea: Worsen: use bits that disturb their neighbours (row hammer, stray fields) so cells must sit far apart. Flip: store the bit in the Neel vector of a chiral antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn or CuMnAs) switched by ns spin-orbit current pulses and read by anomalous Hall or tunnel magnetoresistance; antiferromagnets have no stray field and THz dynamics, so cells pack at minimum pitch and ignore neighbour activity.
why: Row-hammer immunity (fact 9), no refresh (fact 3), ps-ns writes; avoids the stray-field pitch limit of ferromagnetic MRAM.

title: Fremen stillsuit: SiGe quantum-well hole cell, recaptured supercritical CO2
idea: A Fremen stillsuit recovers every molecule. Holes are stored in a buried Ge-rich SiGe quantum well under the access channel, a capacitor built into the band structure, where a valence-band barrier slows leakage. Every clean and dry uses supercritical CO2 with a co-solvent, distilled and reused in a closed loop.
why: A capacitor-less cell (facts 1, 2) with retention boosted by the heterostructure (fact 3). Supercritical CO2 replaces DI rinse and dry and is more than 95% recycled, for more than 10x less water.

title: Po: the bit runs forever — kinetic-inductance fluxon nanowire loops
idea: Po: the bit is a current that runs forever. Extracted: ~100 nm NbN nanowire loops whose kinetic inductance (~100x geometric) lets one flux quantum be held in a tiny loop at 4 K; the bit is the direction of the persistent current, read by a shunted nanowire switch, as working memory for cryogenic AI racks.
why: Zero leakage and aJ-scale switching for cryo compute; loop area far below classic SQUID memory cells. Needs 4 K and NbN film uniformity.

title: Storage layer on the backside power network of U.S. logic
idea: Box = {medium: charge on BEOL MIM capacitors | access: low-temperature Zn-based oxide TFTs | sense: SAs in the front-side logic | integration: memory tier built on the wafer backside after backside-power processing, plate tied to the backside power mesh | substrate: U.S.-made leading-edge logic wafers (Arizona/Oregon) | fab: <400 C backside ALD}. The thinned backside otherwise carries only power rails; a 1T1C tier there puts several MB per mm2 directly under the compute with sub-micron vertical paths.
why: Fact 5 data-movement energy (~10x below HBM) and U.S. manufacturability: memory capacity from domestic leading-edge logic fabs that already exist.

title: Plasma-panel wall-charge memory shrunk to sealed field-emission nanogaps
idea: AC plasma displays (PLATO, 1964) had inherent memory: wall charge left on the dielectric keeps a fired cell firing under a common sustain wave while unfired cells stay dark. Replace the gas discharge with field emission across 20-nm sealed dielectric-coated nanogaps; a global sustain AC re-deposits wall charge each half-cycle only in 'on' cells, and X/Y address pulses add or erase wall charge.
why: The hysteresis itself is the selector, so the crosspoint is 4F2 and stackable; the global sustain is built-in refresh with no row activations, which also removes row hammer (Facts 3, 8, 9).

title: Air-gap NEMS relay replaces the leaky access transistor
idea: IFR: an access switch whose off-state is perfect emptiness. Closest achievable: a vertical nanoelectromechanical relay (TiN cantilever, ~5 nm air gap) gates each storage capacitor; off-state leakage is tunnelling through air (<1e-21 A), so today's 5 fF capacitor holds charge for minutes to hours.
why: Fact 3: removes the <=13 fA tail and refresh power; with retention solved, Cs can fall 5-10x and break the aspect-ratio wall (fact 1). Contact endurance is the main risk.

title: Rust: hematite antiferromagnet switched by orbital torque, no heavy metals
idea: Stimulus 'rust' -> use alpha-Fe2O3 (hematite), an insulating antiferromagnet, as the bit: its Neel vector is rotated by orbital-Hall torque from a light Ti or Cr layer instead of Pt or W spin-Hall metals, and read by spin-Hall magnetoresistance. Stacks are sputtered and Ar-ion-milled, so no fluorine etch.
why: Nonvolatile, ps-switching, field-immune bit with no refresh (fact 3) and immunity to row-hammer coupling (fact 9), made from iron oxide and avoiding tungsten (China ~80%) and platinum-group metals.

title: Fe: hematite Néel-vector bit flipped by titanium orbital torque
idea: Store the bit in the Néel vector of a ~5 nm alpha-Fe2O3 island, switch it with orbital-Hall current from an adjacent Ti strip (light-metal orbital torque instead of Pt/W spin-Hall), and read it by spin-Hall magnetoresistance or a stacked tunnel junction; antiferromagnetic order has no stray field and switches in picoseconds.
why: Non-volatile, field-immune, unlimited-endurance cell removes refresh (fact 3) and neighbor disturb (fact 9) using only Fe, Ti and O; a read signal of ~0.1-1% is the hurdle.

title: Gun-bluing rust bit: oxidized-iron antiferromagnet switched by orbital torque
idea: Borrow gun bluing, the controlled oxidation of steel: thermally oxidize Fe films into epitaxial alpha-Fe2O3 (hematite) nanodots whose Neel vector is the bit. A Cr/CuOx line underneath switches it by orbital Hall torque, and spin-Hall magnetoresistance reads it.
why: Antiferromagnets have no stray field (<=10 nm pitch) and THz dynamics (sub-ns write). Unlimited endurance and no refresh from iron rust, chromium and copper, with no Pt, Co or Ta.

title: Thermally locked ionic glass gating: ions frozen between writes
idea: Combine electric-double-layer ionic gating with a glass transition: the gate dielectric is an ionic glass whose ions move only above ~120 C, so a nanoscale heater line warms one cell for ~10 ns to drive ions and set the channel charge, and on cooling the ions freeze in place. The channel conductance stores the bit with no hold power.
why: Zero refresh; EDL gating gives ~1e14 cm-2 charge density for a large read signal; thermal write energy and speed are risks.

title: Setting gelatin: glass-transition-locked ions freeze a double-layer bit
idea: Like gelatin that flows warm and sets cold, spin-coat a polymerized ionic liquid (Tg ~60-80 C) as the gate dielectric of a thin channel: a ns local heater pulse lifts it above Tg, the gate voltage forms an electric double layer (~10 uF/cm2), and on cooling the ions freeze in place, holding a doping-like state with no electronic leakage path; read is the channel conductance.
why: Retention without access-transistor leakage (the charge sits in immobile ions) plus giant areal capacitance for tiny cells; made with spin coater, e-beam and evaporator; thermal crosstalk and ~10s of fJ heating per write are the risks.

title: Capacitor first, transistor last: bonded perovskite capacitor wafer
idea: Reverse fabrication order: build a planar BST/SrTiO3 capacitor array first and crystallize it at 700 C (k ~300, the 1990s gigabit-DRAM dielectric), then smart-cut bond (1995) a pre-implanted thin silicon layer on top and finish 180 nm access transistors below 450 C so the perovskite never sees transistor hazards.
why: Charge wall and capital (facts 1,4): planar 0.2 um2 x ~100 fF/um2 ~ 20 fF with no deep etch; tiers repeat by further bonds; risk is hydrogen damage to the perovskite and bond overlay.

title: Printed metal-insulator-metal tunnel diode replaces access transistor
idea: IFR: an access device that is only a sandwich. Closest achievable: use a printed Ta2O5 or Al2O3 MIM diode, as in early active-matrix LCDs, as a two-terminal nonlinear access device for each printed storage capacitor; strong I-V nonlinearity isolates half-selected cells.
why: Facts 7 and 4: two-terminal printed access removes TFT gate layers, giving a printable 4F^2 crosspoint cell.

title: Mask-selected ferroelectric phase makes hybrid volatile and persistent mats
idea: Industrial controllers want working memory that snapshots on power loss; a thin Si- or La-oxide dopant sublayer is deposited blanket before the ZrO2 dielectric and the single added mask strips it from ordinary mats, so on anneal the doped mats crystallize orthorhombic (ferroelectric) and the rest tetragonal (linear high-k). One die carries DRAM mats and persistent ferroelectric mats from one flow.
why: Puts non-volatile snapshot capacity on the DRAM die, removing separate backup memory and enabling instant-on; uniform dopant coverage in 60:1 pillars is the challenge.

title: Lowdin tautomer bit: proton-transfer hydrogen-bond ferroelectric layer
idea: DNA base pairs can flip protons across their hydrogen bonds (Lowdin tautomers). Use a proton-transfer organic ferroelectric, such as croconic acid or a designed base-pair-analog crystal, whose polarization flips when protons hop ~0.6 A along the H-bonds with no heavy-ion motion. It serves as a ferroelectric capacitor or FeFET gate layer.
why: Non-volatile, deposited from solution below 150 C, with no Hf/Zr. Light protons promise <10 ns switching and low fatigue; croconic acid shows ~20-30 uC/cm2 at room temperature.

title: Long-channel thick-oxide gain cell in open-source 130 nm
idea: MAGNIFY channel length ~10x and oxide thickness ~3x on the write device: a 3T gain cell in the open SKY130/GF180 PDKs uses the 5 V thick-oxide transistor as write switch (aA subthreshold leakage) and stores on the read transistor's gate; free or cheap shuttles allow monthly iterations.
why: Retention ~1-10 s vs 64 ms (fact 3) in U.S.-fabbed nodes with near-zero capital; niche embedded DRAM for chiplets.

title: Baikonur launch engineer: topotactic SrCoOx oxygen-sponge bit, ion-milled
idea: An engineer under embargo at Baikonur makes do on the dry steppe. Store the bit as the phase of SrCoOx: brownmillerite SrCoO2.5 (insulating) or perovskite SrCoO3 (metallic), switched by a gate pulse that pumps oxygen in from an adjacent reservoir layer. The stack is sputtered and patterned by ion milling with an in-situ sidewall clean.
why: Phase switching with large resistance contrast and room for multi-level storage (fact 4). There is no wet etch or clean, a more than 10x water cut; cobalt supply is a risk.

title: Single-implant gated-diode amplifying cell for $1 IoT microcontrollers
idea: A $1 IoT MCU in 40 nm logic needs megabytes of RAM without a capacitor module; one added implant mask forms a gated diode whose gate capacitance is large when '1' is stored (inverted) and tiny when '0', so boosting the gate during read amplifies the '1' several-fold (2T1D cell). Everything else uses existing logic layers.
why: ~3x denser-than-SRAM embedded working memory for one mask, cutting MCU die cost; the self-amplifying node needs ~5x less Cs (fact 1).

title: Orbital Hall torque from chromium writes magnets without tungsten or platinum
idea: Effect walk: orbital Hall effect. Replace W/Pt/Ta spin-Hall write lines in SOT magnetic cells with light 3d metals (Cr, Ti, V) whose orbital Hall conductivity is predicted ~10x Pt's spin Hall conductivity, converting the orbital current to torque through a 1-nm Ni or Gd conversion layer under the free layer.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and platinum from the write path and may cut write current 2-5x, making SOT-class DRAM-replacement cells cheaper in scarce-resource terms.

title: Farmer grows memory: croconic-acid proton-tautomer ferroelectric storage layer
idea: A farmer asks why memory can't be grown. Croconic acid, a small organic molecule, is ferroelectric at room temperature (Pr ~20 uC/cm2) because its protons hop between oxygen atoms; vapor-deposit it as the storage layer of a 1T1C cell instead of using mined Hf/Zr.
why: Removes the Hf/Zr dependence and allows low-temperature BEOL deposition; per area, the switched polarization charge is ~20x what a dielectric capacitor holds (fact 1).

title: Eliminate analog sensing: Coulomb-blockade dots hold quantized electron counts
idea: Eliminate the continuous charge level: store 0, 1, 2 or 3 extra electrons on a ~2-nm silicon or metal nanodot whose charging energy (>150 meV, ~6 kT) quantizes the stored charge, so each cell holds 2 bits as discrete states read by an integrated single-electron-transistor electrometer.
why: 2 bits per tiny cell (fact 1, density) with attojoule writes (fact 10); thick barriers make it refresh-free; risk is room-temperature operation needing sub-2-nm uniformity and offset-charge noise.

title: Synaptic-vesicle quantal storage: Coulomb-staircase multilevel node
idea: Synapses release transmitter in fixed quanta. Make the storage node a sub-3 nm metal island (e.g. an Au cluster in SiO2) whose >100 meV charging energy quantizes stored charge into discrete electron-number plateaus. A single-electron-transistor sense node writes and reads four robust levels per cell, so the levels are set by physics rather than analog trimming.
why: Density and cost per bit: 2 bits per cell from built-in quantization, and the tiny node removes the capacitor. The main risk is room-temperature background charge noise.

title: Room-temperature single-electron box with electrometer readout
idea: Scale down to counting electrons: store tens of electrons on a sub-3 nm silicon or metal nanocluster whose charging energy exceeds kT at 300 K, read by an adjacent single-electron transistor whose current jumps with each electron.
why: Energy and density: write energy near aJ, cell footprint ~10 nm, attacking CV2 voltage floor.

title: Single-electron Coulomb-blockade node read by an on-cell SET
idea: Effect walk: Coulomb blockade. Store the bit as 0 vs ~10 electrons on a 3-nm Si dot whose ~150 meV charging energy quantizes occupancy, written through a tunnel barrier at ~0.2 V and read by a co-integrated single-electron transistor whose current swings ~100x per added electron.
why: Moves ~10 electrons instead of ~30,000 (5 fF x 1 V) and the SET gain lets the bitline swing only ~50 mV: ~100x lower cell+bitline energy per access (fact 10), and the Coulomb gap suppresses leakage (fact 3); room-temperature SET variability is the risk.

title: Quipu knots: topological polar textures as unknottable bits
idea: Inca quipu stored data in knots that cannot untie by accident; store a bit as the topological charge of a polar skyrmion or vortex in a 20-nm oxide-superlattice nanodisk (PbTiO3/SrTiO3, or lead-free BaTiO3/SrTiO3), which cannot relax continuously to the trivial state, switched by a field pulse from a top tip electrode and read by its distinct capacitance or tunneling conductance.
why: Facts 1 and 3: density set by texture size (~10 nm) rather than capacitor charge, and topology gives non-volatility without fatigue-prone domain-wall sweeps; write fields, read contrast and RT stability at 10 nm are unproven.

title: Polar skyrmion topological charge as an unforgettable bit
idea: IFR: a bit that thermal noise cannot flip because it is topologically protected. Closest achievable: in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices, nucleate or annihilate a ~10 nm polar skyrmion with a local electrode field and read its presence through its distinct local permittivity or piezoresponse.
why: Density (~10 nm bits, below 4F^2) and retention without refresh (fact 3); no ion motion so endurance is effectively unlimited; sidesteps capacitor scaling (fact 1).

title: Po: a thermometer stuck halfway — spin-crossover molecular bits
idea: Po: a thermometer stuck halfway. Extracted: hold an iron-triazole spin-crossover film (solution-synthesised by the kg, hysteresis ~345-385 K) at ~365 K inside its loop; a Joule pulse switches a cell to high-spin, a piezo pressure pulse switches it back (low-spin is ~10% smaller), and the conductance/permittivity difference is read.
why: A blanket-printed molecular film with no transistors drives cost per GB toward printing cost (>100x below DRAM). Trade-offs: us-ms switching, elevated operating temperature, per-cell piezo addressing.

title: League-table standings: rank-modulated bits immune to uniform charge loss
idea: A league table cares who is ahead, not absolute points: group six cells and encode data in the permutation order of their charges (rank modulation), written by charging each cell just above the previous one and read by a winner-take-all comparator tree; uniform leakage shrinks all charges together without changing the order.
why: Fact 3 and density: refresh is needed only when leakage differences flip an order, ~3-10x longer intervals, and log2(6!)=9.5 bits per 6 cells gives ~1.6 bits/cell (~1.5x density) at the cost of a comparator tree in the sense amp.

title: Thermally drawn fiber preforms yield coaxial capacitor bundles
idea: Adapt optical-fiber drawing: build a macroscopic preform of metal/glass/metal coaxial rods, draw it ~1000x down to 30 nm features over km lengths, slice it into thin wafers of parallel coaxial capacitors, and hybrid-bond them onto access-transistor wafers.
why: Facts 1 and 4: any aspect ratio for the price of drawing glass, with no HAR etch or EUV in the capacitor; registration to transistors is the main risk.

title: Preform-drawn coax capacitor wafers: draw, bundle, redraw, then slice
idea: Borrow optical-fiber drawing. Build a macroscopic preform (Zn-Sn alloy core, BaTiO3-loaded glass dielectric, metal outer shell), then thermally draw, stack and redraw it down to ~30 nm cores. Wafer-thin slices of the bundle carry billions of parallel coax capacitors, which are hybrid-bonded onto the transistor wafer.
why: Fact 1 and capital intensity: capacitor length equals slice thickness (um), not an etched hole, so each coax exceeds 5 fF with no litho or etch. A draw tower replaces a fab for the capacitor wafer.

title: Po: flash that forgets on purpose — direct-tunnel volatile charge-trap tier
idea: Po: flash memory that forgets on purpose. Extracted: change the 3D NAND recipe to a 1.5-2.5 nm tunnel oxide so writes use low-field direct tunnelling (no Fowler-Nordheim damage, endurance >1e12) and accept 1-10 s retention; run idle NAND fab capacity in a down-cycle as a second-tier DRAM refreshed every second.
why: NAND-like ~$0.05-0.1/GB (about 100x below DRAM contract) from existing fabs with no new tools. Trade-offs: 100s of ns to us reads and background refresh every few seconds.

title: Persistent spectral hole burning: a thousand frequency bits per spot
idea: IBM's 1978 PHB patent stored bits as narrow holes burned at chosen frequencies in an inhomogeneously broadened absorption line. Use room-temperature PHB films (Sm2+ in BaFCl-type hosts) where each diffraction-limited spot holds ~1000 frequency channels, written and read by a fast chirped laser and photodiode.
why: Frequency becomes a third storage dimension (~1000x bits per spot) without lithography (Fact 4); erase endurance and speed unproven, so a speculative capacity tier.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric van der Waals bilayer as fatigue-free gain gate
idea: Scarcity rule: no domain-wall pinning defects allowed. Use a sliding ferroelectric (rhombohedral bilayer MoS2 or parallel-stacked hBN), whose polarization flips by a one-third-lattice interlayer slip rather than ion displacement, as the gate of a 2D-channel read transistor; the dangling-bond-free vdW interface removes the charge trapping that limits HfO2 FeFETs.
why: 1T nondestructive-read cell with no capacitor (facts 1, 8) aiming for >1e15 cycles because sliding involves no oxygen-vacancy migration; needs wafer-scale aligned bilayers.

title: Via-programmed ROM for frozen model weights frees DRAM
idea: Combine mask-ROM economics with AI inference: weights frozen for a product's life are encoded in one via layer (1-2F2 per bit, multi-level via resistance for 2 bits) on a die whose other masks are shared, so only the via mask changes per model, written by e-beam or DUV. The weights never need refresh, never wear out, and stop occupying HBM.
why: Weights are a large share of inference memory; moving them to refresh-free ROM at ~1/5 the cost per bit releases that DRAM supply.

title: Single-proton tautomer molecules as one-nanometer dipole bits
idea: Self-assemble a monolayer of porphycene-type molecules whose inner hydrogen pair hops between two nitrogen sites, with substituents tuning the proton double-well barrier to ~0.8 eV for >=1 s retention. A gate pulse flips the ~100 tautomers under a 10x10 nm electrode, and their collective dipole shifts the threshold of a 2D-channel read transistor.
why: From first principles, the smallest object with a room-temperature-grade barrier is one proton in a double well (~1 nm3). Storage density is then limited only by addressing, at aJ switching energy, with no capacitor (fact 1) or charge leakage (fact 3).

title: Nanorelay-gated storage node with effectively infinite off-resistance
idea: MAGNIFY access-device off-resistance to infinity: replace the access transistor with a ~1 ns, 15-nm-gap NEMS contact switch (Ru or TiN cantilever) so the storage node is isolated by a gas gap when open and only the capacitor dielectric leaks.
why: Kills the leakage tail (fact 3) for hours-to-days retention and lowers wordline voltage via ~1 V pull-in (fact 10); contacts must survive ~1e14 cycles.

title: Glow-in-the-dark phosphor traps: optically erased deep-trap charge bit
idea: Persistent phosphors (SrAl2O4:Eu,Dy) hold electrons in Dy-type traps for hours; dope a thin wide-gap film over a readout channel with one engineered deep trap (~1.0-1.3 eV), fill it electrically through a thin barrier, and empty it with a sub-ns pulse from an integrated micro-LED/waveguide (optically stimulated detrapping, as in OSL dosimeters) instead of high-field tunneling erase.
why: Fact 3: deep-trap retention of seconds to hours removes most refresh, and avoiding Fowler-Nordheim erase stress is the bet for flash-beating endurance (>=1e12); optical routing area and write speed are open questions.

title: Antiferroelectric-knee capacitor biased onto ZrO2's steep switching branch
idea: Box = {medium: field-induced polarization in antiferroelectric ZrO2 | access: vertical-channel Si FET | sense: standard charge-share SA | integration: 1T1C with a short pillar | substrate: 300 mm Si | fab: ALD ZrO2/Al2O3 nanolaminate}. The cell plate is DC-biased just below the AFE-to-FE critical field so the +/-0.5 V node swing rides the steep double-hysteresis branch, where dQ/dV equals an effective k of ~100-150; the cell runs minor loops and never reaches full remanent switching, which limits fatigue.
why: Fact 1 capacitor charge wall: 3-5x charge per area lets pillar AR fall from ~70:1 to ~20:1, removing the hardest etch and allowing a tighter pitch.

title: VO2 bistable inside its thermal hysteresis, erased by piezo-AlN strain
idea: Box = {medium: metallic vs insulating phase of VO2 held inside its hysteresis loop at a 65 C die temperature | access: Si FET | sense: ~100x resistance ratio | integration: VO2 on a piezoelectric AlN underlayer | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: sputtered VO2 from Utah vanadium}. A Joule pulse writes the metallic phase, and a strain pulse from the AlN underlayer shifts the transition temperature above the die temperature so the cell snaps back to insulating; at idle both phases are stable with no power.
why: Facts 3 and 10: no refresh, an all-domestic V/Al/N/Si stack, and it uses the heat DRAM dies already run at.

title: Siberian permafrost engineer: 77 K SrTiO3 quantum-paraelectric capacitor
idea: A Siberian engineer treats cold as a free resource. Run the memory immersed in liquid nitrogen, where SrTiO3's quantum-paraelectric permittivity climbs into the thousands and access-transistor leakage falls by more than 1e6. A flat planar capacitor then holds enough charge, and refresh happens hours apart.
why: Removes the high-AR capacitor (fact 1) and nearly all refresh (fact 3); the planar cell cuts EUV and etch steps (fact 4). The price is cryocooling at the rack.

title: Titanium-submarine engineer: Hf-free rutile TiO2 templated on RuO2
idea: A Soviet engineer who built titanium-hulled submarines uses the metal his country has in plenty. Grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k~90-110) templated on RuO2 bottom electrodes below 400 C, with Al doping to tame leakage, in place of HfO2/ZrO2 stacks.
why: Meets fact 1's k~70+ target, so the same Cs comes from a lower-AR pillar, and removes the hafnium and zirconium dependence; ruthenium supply is the remaining risk.

title: Vacuum-gap tunneling floating node: oxide-free, wear-free charge storage
idea: Separate a floating metal node from its write electrode by a 2-2.5 nm vacuum gap, made by ashing a sacrificial ALD carbon layer in O2 plasma at <=250 C. Write by direct or field-emission tunneling through vacuum (~ns at 2-3 V); retention is set by gap width because tunneling is exponential in it (2.5 nm gives >1 s).
why: Oxide wear-out needs a lattice to damage and vacuum has none, so this targets unlimited endurance for a floating-node store. No capacitor pillar (fact 1), and the cell stacks in BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Four-level DRAM cell using flash-style program-and-verify
idea: Combine NAND flash's incremental-step program-and-verify loop with DRAM charge storage: the write driver applies short pulses and senses the node between pulses until it lands in one of four charge windows, storing 2 bits per cell. A gain read device and a reference ladder resolve the levels, and refresh re-centers each level.
why: Density and cost per bit (fact 4): 2x bits/cell without a node shrink, worth several nodes of 10-20% scaling; write latency roughly doubles.

title: Conducting ferroelectric domain walls as switchable nanoscale wires
idea: Effect walk: domain-wall conduction. In a thin-film LiNbO3 or ErMnO3 cell, a written charged domain wall bridging two electrodes conducts ~10^4x better than the bulk; short pulses inject or erase the wall to store the bit, and a 0.1-V read through the wall leaves polarization untouched.
why: A non-destructive 0.1-V read with large margin removes the restore cycle and full-rail bitline charging (facts 8, 10), cutting read energy >10x; the wall is ~1 nm wide, so density is set by lithography, not physics.

title: Sell retention-fallout dies as permanent fast-refresh DDR5 SKUs
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): standard controllers only. Dies that miss 64 ms retention because of a weak-cell tail are fused to always report the hot-temperature refresh-rate code (2x or 4x refresh) in the existing MR4 register, so stock controllers refresh them faster, and they sell at a discount into capacity-hungry, bandwidth-tolerant tiers such as CXL expanders and inference KV-cache.
why: Recovers a few percent of wafer output now scrapped or downbinned, raising usable bit supply immediately with zero capex (cost per bit, supply).

title: Si: buried-channel CCD charge loops replace per-bit access transistors
idea: Store bits as charge packets circulating in 64-256-stage buried-channel silicon CCD loops clocked by three-phase gates (the 1970s CCD-memory idea revived at 12 nm), with one injector and one sense node per loop; charge-transfer loss and dark current are allowed to reach ~1% packet errors per circuit, corrected by a per-loop code.
why: No access transistor, contact or capacitor per bit (facts 1, 3, 7): a stage is just overlapping gates; the 1% budget allows faster clocking and longer loops, so average access stays ~30-60 ns.

title: Contactless bistable buckled nanobeam snaps between two shapes
idea: Shrink the hair-clip snap-through to a 100 nm single-crystal SiC beam pre-buckled by film stress: the bit is up or down buckling, flipped electrostatically and read by piezoresistance, and it never touches a contact so it avoids stiction.
why: Endurance and leakage: nonvolatile, zero standby power, 1e12+ fatigue cycles in single-crystal SiC.

title: Magnetostriction reused: piezo-strain-written nanomagnets on FRAM PZT lines
idea: The magnetostriction behind 1950s delay lines can write bits: place elliptical Galfenol or Terfenol-D nanomagnets on a PZT film using existing 130-nm FRAM PZT tooling, flip them with a voltage-driven strain pulse plus small bias field, and read with an AMR/GMR stack sputtered in the same BEOL.
why: aJ-class current-free writes break the CV2 floor (Fact 10), non-volatile (Fact 3), no capacitor (Fact 1); uses existing PZT and magnetic sputter tools.

title: 3D NAND strings retuned for DRAM retention and endurance
idea: Time-shift flash from 10-year retention to ~1 s: thin the tunnel oxide to 1.5-2 nm direct tunneling so charge traps in a 200-tier vertical string write in ns with 1e15 cycles, refreshed like DRAM, using existing 3D NAND fabs.
why: Capital intensity and density: 200 stacked tiers built with mature NAND tools and no EUV, multi-x bits per mm2.

title: Chocolate-tempered rutile TiO2: seed crystals select the k~100 polymorph
idea: Chocolatiers add Form-V cocoa-butter seed crystals to force the right crystal form. Here a 2 nm rutile-structured beta-MnO2 (or F:SnO2) seed on a TiN electrode, plus a tempering anneal cycle, forces TiO2 to crystallize as rutile (k~90-110) instead of anatase (k~40) at <=450 C, with no RuO2 template.
why: Fact 1: about 2-2.5x today's ZrO2 k using only Ti, Mn and O. Removes the Ru dependence of rutile-TiO2 DRAM capacitors.

title: Shape-memory 'training' bit: Ni-Mn-Sn martensite twin variant stores data
idea: Copy how shape-memory-alloy wire is trained: train a Ni-Mn-Sn Heusler nanodot so its martensite settles in one of two twin variants. Gate-applied strain or field flips the variant diffusionlessly, with no atomic migration, and magnetic or resistive anisotropy reads it.
why: Ferroelastic storage from Ni, Mn and Sn with no charge leakage (fact 3). Diffusionless switching aims at >1e12 cycles.

title: Thin-film flux-closure nanorings: magnetic core memory reborn
idea: Combine 1960s ferrite core memory with thin-film lithography: each bit is a 50-100 nm CoFeB ring whose vortex magnetization circulates clockwise or counterclockwise, switched by a current pulse through a central via and read by a TMR sensor at the ring edge. Closed flux means no stray field between neighbours and no refresh.
why: Zero refresh and unlimited endurance (no tunnel barrier in the write path), radiation hard, 6-10F2 cells.

title: Swap charge for ferroelastic twin variant read by piezoresistance
idea: Store the bit as which of two ferroelastic twin orientations a nanocrystal adopts (for example tetragonal-twin BiFeO3 or a NiTi martensite nanopillar). A strain pulse from an integrated AlN piezo layer switches it, and the read uses the anisotropic piezoresistance of an underlying channel.
why: Non-volatile with non-destructive read (facts 3, 8); voltage-driven at <0.5 V through piezo coupling (fact 10).

title: HP rotaxane crossbar fixed: molecular shuttles locked in a MOF lattice
idea: HP/UCLA rotaxane crossbars failed because evaporated top metal punched through the soft monolayer, so the 'switching' was really filaments. Grow a thin rigid metal-organic framework whose linkers are bistable [2]rotaxanes, so each ring shuttles between two stations inside a stiff pore, and laminate a transferred graphene top electrode so no metal atoms enter.
why: Molecular-scale bits (~100 shuttles per cell ensemble), nonvolatile with no refresh, low-temperature and stackable in BEOL.

title: Optane without melting: MnTe crystal-to-crystal polymorph switching
idea: Optane's melt-quench writes burned energy, and its amorphous state drifted and recrystallized when hot. Switch MnTe between its NiAs-type and wurtzite-type crystalline polymorphs through a displacive transition with no melting: both states are crystals, so neither drifts nor crystallizes at 125 C, and the polymorphs show a large reported resistance contrast.
why: 10-year retention above 125 C with an estimated 3-10x lower write energy than melting and no resistance drift, so multi-level storage becomes viable.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch storing bits at a quarter volt
idea: MINIFY hold voltage to ~0.25 V: two series Esaki band-to-band tunnel diodes grown as a vertical Ge/Si or GaSb/InAs stack form a bistable midpoint node (Goto pair) behind one access transistor, holding a static bit with ~10 pA standby and no refresh.
why: Escapes the ~1 V VARY / CV2 floor (fact 10) and refresh (fact 3); vertical diode stacking keeps area near 1T1C.

title: 2D interband tunnel-diode Goto pair: static bit with picoamp hold
idea: Scarcity rule: zero hold power and nothing above 1 V. Two series interband tunnel diodes (broken-gap black-phosphorus/SnSe2 vdW junctions with peak-to-valley ratio >100) form a bistable midpoint node held at valley current, and one access transistor reads and writes it like an SRAM half-cell.
why: Static storage removes refresh (fact 3) in 1T plus two stacked diodes (~8F2 vs 120-150F2 SRAM) and runs below 0.5 V, breaking the 1 V VARY floor (fact 10); valley current must fall below ~10 pA per cell.

title: Two-hundred-variant bit-cell zoo on every shuttle run
idea: MAGNIFY variants and MINIFY cost per experiment: tile 200 bit-cell variants (gain cells, varactor caps, bootstrapped switches, leakage latches) with on-die retention/endurance BIST on each $10-20k MPW shuttle, publish an open retention-tail database and license the winners.
why: Cuts cell-discovery cycles from years to quarters and feeds U.S. fabs with characterized cells (facts 3, 4).

title: JEDEC heal command and storage-cell health telemetry standard
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: standardize a host-visible cell-health report (per-mat retention-tail percentiles) plus a REJUV command class (thermal, detox pulse, spare swap), so the OS can schedule storage-element repair the way SSDs schedule TRIM and garbage collection; CHIPS-funded buyers require it in procurement.
why: Repairability at fleet scale: turns per-device heal mechanisms into a usable ecosystem, extending module life.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal at 400 C erasing the leakage tail
idea: The <=13 fA retention-tail cells come from trap-assisted tunneling through a few interface and junction dangling bonds. A 20 atm D2 anneal at 400 C passivates them, and the Si-D bond resists hot-carrier and field depassivation several times better than Si-H, cutting the tail at its physical source.
why: Pushing the tail out 10x stretches refresh intervals 2-4x, saving ~50-75% of refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) with one anneal step that fits existing fabs.

title: Seed bank: national shuttle wafers for wild storage-element candidates
idea: Stimulus 'seed bank' -> a CHIPS-funded 300 mm back-end shuttle where any lab drops a candidate storage stack into a standard 1T1X 1 Mb test array four times a year, with shared ns-pulse testers, 10^15-cycle endurance rigs and open retention-tail data. One-off device papers become array statistics in 6 months.
why: Cuts the time and capital to qualify a new bit element from years and ~$50M to months and ~$100k (capital/time chokepoint), seeding U.S. memory manufacturability.

title: Antiferroelectric transition boosts stored charge in standard 1T1C
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): same 1T1C array, sense amps and timings. Replace the ZrO2 dielectric with a tuned antiferroelectric ZrO2/HfZrO film and bias the plate so the 0-to-VARY swing crosses the field-induced AFE-to-FE transition, whose extra polarization charge gives an effective k above 100; the film relaxes back on discharge with no remanence or wake-up.
why: 2-3x Cs at the same AR (fact 1), or today's Cs at ~30:1; reversible AFE transitions avoid domain pinning, targeting >1e15 cycles with unchanged timings.

title: EDSAC-style delay loops rebuilt as WDM light on photonics foundries
idea: Recirculate bits as light in low-loss SiN spiral loops on existing 45/90-nm silicon-photonics foundry lines (such as AIM Photonics), with 32 WDM channels at 50 Gb/s and an SOA plus clock-recovery regenerator per loop.
why: 1.6 Tb/s x 20 ns loop holds 32 kb with <=20 ns latency: DRAM-class access, no cells, and optical I/O straight to accelerators (Fact 5); energy per regeneration pass is the risk.

title: Hysteretic Mott latch: niobium dioxide cell held inside its loop
idea: IFR: a cell that latches itself with no transistor and no capacitor. Closest achievable: bias a nanoscale NbO2 device through a series resistor at a hold voltage inside its insulator-metal hysteresis window so either phase is stable; a short over- or under-voltage pulse flips it and reading senses the ~10^3 resistance ratio.
why: Facts 1 and 7: a one-element 4F^2 volatile latch with no capacitor, ns switching and no filament wear-out.

title: Qualification by kinetic-crossover hunting, not single-Arrhenius extrapolation
idea: Several dead memories (early PCM, CBRAM) passed high-temperature bakes but failed in the field because a second, lower-activation-energy failure path dominated at use conditions. Require bakes at five temperatures (125-250 C) plus Kissinger ramp analysis to detect kinetic crossover, and design storage elements with at least 0.3 eV margin between competing mechanisms.
why: Prevents the late qualification failures that kill ventures and makes the 125 C/10 y guarantee credible early in development.

title: Unity CMOx fixed: swap slow oxygen ions for nanosecond protons
idea: Unity Semiconductor's CMOx, which exchanged oxygen ions between oxide layers, died from slow, high-voltage switching. Shuttle protons instead, through a phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte into a WO3 channel: high-field proton insertion has shown ns programming, and conductance is read without disturbance.
why: ns low-energy writes with analog multi-level states (2-4 bits per cell gives density); BEOL-compatible.

title: Let the electrode become the dielectric: anodized metal-sponge capacitors
idea: Reverse deposition: oblique-sputter a porous aluminum or niobium sponge into each 180 nm cell, then anodize it so the metal converts itself into conformal Al2O3 or Nb2O5 (k ~41) that self-limits at ~2 nm per volt even inside hidden pores; fill with CVD TiN as the counter electrode, like an electrolytic capacitor.
why: Charge wall (fact 1) with a wet 1900s-era process: ~10-30x surface gain per footprint, no ALD or EUV, abundant Al/Nb; risk is anodic oxide leakage and pore filling.

title: Williams tube 2.0: on-chip field-emitter arrays writing a charge mosaic
idea: Like the Williams-Kilburn CRT that stored bits as charge spots on a phosphor face, a vacuum-sealed micro-cavity holds a carbon-nanotube field-emitter array, each emitter electrostatically deflected over a 4x4 um patch of a nitride charge-trap mosaic. Bits are 20-nm trapped-charge spots written by beam dose and read by secondary-electron yield on re-scan, with write-back exactly like the Williams regeneration raster.
why: No wire, transistor or capacitor per bit: periphery is per-emitter not per-row (Fact 7) and bits are not litho-defined (Fact 4); ~40k bits per emitter gives ~5 Gb/cm2 per layer from old-node litho; beam slew ~20-50 ns.

title: Stacked antiferroelectric staircase capacitor stores three charge levels
idea: Downlink-limited imaging satellites value capacity per gram; the capacitor dielectric becomes a bilayer of two antiferroelectric films with different switching fields (ZrO2 and Hf-doped ZrO2), yielding a staircase charge-voltage curve with three flat plateaus, so each cell holds 1.58 bits with wide margins. The only added mask restores the old dielectric for periphery decoupling capacitors.
why: ~1.5x bits per pillar (density, cost per bit); plateaus give better multi-level margins than linear analog levels.

title: SiC deep-depletion inversion-charge cell with hour-long retention
idea: Box = {medium: minority-carrier inversion charge under a SiC MOS gate | access: lateral SiC transfer gate | sense: charge transfer to a floating diffusion + source follower | integration: dedicated SiC memory die bonded to Si logic | substrate: U.S.-made 200 mm 4H-SiC (North Carolina/New York) | fab: U.S. SiC power-device lines}. SiC's 3.26 eV bandgap cuts thermal generation by ~1e-18 relative to silicon, so a deep-depletion well holds charge for hours at 85 C; it is the original inversion-layer 1T DRAM concept, minus refresh.
why: Fact 3: refresh disappears (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth), using U.S. SiC capacity that swings with power-device demand.

title: N: volatile SONOS with 1.5 nm tunnel oxide, direct-tunnel writes
idea: Thin the SONOS bottom oxide to ~1.5 nm so electrons enter the Si3N4 trap layer by direct tunneling in ~10 ns at ~2 V (no Fowler-Nordheim damage, so endurance can approach 1e12+), accept ~seconds retention with ~1% early-decay cells, and refresh at that interval.
why: Capacitorless 1T storage (facts 1, 2) from the most standard fab materials, stackable in 3D NAND-like strings; the 1% budget sets the refresh interval by the bulk, not the worst-case tail.

title: Swap 30,000-electron capacitor for 200-electron node plus single-electron sensor
idea: Shrink the storage node to a ~0.03 fF gate island and read it with a room-temperature silicon single-electron transistor shared by a few cells. The transistor's sub-3-nm dot is formed by a dopant cluster or an oxidised nanowire constriction, and its Coulomb oscillation turns a few-electron change into a large current swing.
why: Breaks the charge wall outright (fact 1): the storage element needs no capacitor, so the cell is planar and easy to stack for 3D (fact 2).

title: Mono-family silicon storage element recyclable straight to solar-grade silicon
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: build the storage element only from Si, SiO2, Si3N4 and doped poly-Si (ONO dielectric, poly electrodes, no Hf/Zr/Ru/W/TiN) and accept the low k by reading with a gain cell instead of charge sharing. Shredded end-of-life dies go straight to silicon refining after an HF strip, with no heavy-metal contamination.
why: Scarce resources and recyclability: removes tungsten (China ~80%), Ru and Hf; gain readout tolerates ~0.5 fF storage.

title: Entatic-state inversion: copper complexes whose geometry change locks electrons
idea: Blue copper proteins tune their geometry (the entatic state) to make electron transfer fast. Invert the trick: choose Cu(I)/Cu(II) complexes whose tetrahedral-to-square-planar change puts a ~1 eV reorganization barrier on spontaneous back-transfer, and place a dense monolayer between channel and gate. A gate pulse overcomes the Marcus barrier in ns, and the trapped charge shifts Vt non-volatilely.
why: Molecular-scale non-volatile charge storage whose retention comes from nuclear reorganization rather than thick tunnel oxides. Writes need low fields, endurance avoids oxide wear, and per-molecule storage could scale density.

title: Charge-plasma junctionless storage node kills GIDL leakage tail
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): unchanged timings and voltages. Remove the doped n+ storage-node junction: the access channel is undoped and the storage-node extension is electrostatically doped by a low-work-function metal (charge plasma), so no metallurgical pn junction remains for junction leakage or GIDL band-to-band tunneling.
why: Shrinks the <=13 fA leakage tail (fact 3) ~10x, stretching retention and cutting refresh via the existing refresh-rate register, while removing implant and anneal steps.

title: Sliding ferroelectric bilayers switch by 1.4 angstrom registry shift
idea: Scale down to van der Waals stacking: in parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or MoS2 the bit is the AB versus BA stacking order, flipped by a sub-angstrom interlayer slide under field, with reported low fatigue because no ions move.
why: Endurance and voltage: sub-1 V switching, 1e10+ cycles target, wafer-scale 2D growth enables BEOL stacking.

title: Printed ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal bit that heals itself
idea: IFR: a ferroelectric that cannot fatigue because it is liquid. Closest achievable: inkjet ferroelectric nematic mesogens (RM734/DIO class, P ~6 uC/cm^2) into printed microwells between printed electrodes; polarization is read capacitively and the fluid order regrows after every switch (us today, targeting ~100 ns in nanowells).
why: Endurance with ferroelectric-class charge, fully printable at low temperature; R2R cost per bit.

title: Complementary oxide-TFT static latch cells on cheap glass panels
idea: Invert 'working memory must be 1T1C DRAM' -> go static where area is cheap. Pair n-type IGZO with p-type SnO or Cu2O TFTs into a 4T loadless or 6T latch on glass whose feedback holds data with zero refresh, while oxide-level leakage keeps standby to ~pW per Mb.
why: No capacitor, no refresh and no destructive read (facts 1, 3, 8) with display tooling; density ~10x below DRAM but panel area makes it a cheap capacity or AI-scratch tier; p-type oxide mobility limits cycle time to ~100 ns.

title: Cold capacitor: quantum paraelectric k~1000 at liquid-nitrogen temperature
idea: Reverse the operating environment: run the array at 77 K, where SrTiO3 or KTaO3 films reach k ~500-2000 and silicon leakage collapses, so the cell capacitor becomes planar or a shallow 5:1 cup, with the memory sharing the accelerator's liquid-nitrogen loop.
why: Charge wall and capital (facts 1,4): 5 fF without the high-AR etch, leakage down >1e6 so refresh effectively vanishes; LN2 cost offset by lower wire resistance.

title: Quantum-paraelectric capacitor whose k explodes in cold pods
idea: Worsen: keep the dielectric constant fixed near 40 and keep etching deeper. Flip: run memory in 40-77 K pods and use quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 or KTaO3 as the cell dielectric, whose k climbs from ~300 to several thousand on cooling, so a planar or shallow-cup capacitor reaches 5 fF at 4F2.
why: Destroys the capacitor charge wall (fact 1: the k ~70 target exceeded >10x) and removes high-AR etch tools (capital, fact 4).

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods shrink the capacitor to planar 1 fF
idea: Borrowing from 77 K cryo-computing users, DRAM dies run immersed in LN2 where trap-assisted and subthreshold leakage fall ~1e6x and sense-amp offsets shrink, so retention reaches minutes. The 60:1 pillar is replaced by a ~1-1.5 fF planar or shallow-cup MIM read on short 64-cell bitlines.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3): HAR etch/deposition steps disappear (~30-50% capacitor-module cost) and refresh power goes to ~0; the ~10 W/W cryocooler overhead must be amortized at rack scale.
